name: Platform-mediated hustle aspiration
description: Late-2010s social-platform exhortations that presented unremitting work as a visible professional identity.
cause_of_death: Contemporary burnout criticism intensified into pandemic-era rejection of overwork as an aspirational status marker; continued use remains documented.

sources.title: Rise and grind
sources.note: Contemporary BBC account identifies rise and grind, hustle harder, and hustle culture as conspicuous worker rhetoric and critiques the burnout beneath it.

sources.title: The 'Rise and Grind' of Hustle Culture
sources.note: Contemporary account criticizes the glorification of overwork; it provides backlash evidence, not annual phrase-frequency measurements.

sources.title: Hustle culture: Is this the end of rise-and-grind?
sources.note: Reports diminished cultural aspiration after pandemic reprioritization; explicitly says the culture has not entirely faded and attests grindset.

entries.gloss: An exhortation to begin the day with relentless productive effort.

examples.text: Rise and grind: please send the completed figures before lunch.

entries.rationale: The 2019 BBC headline and body directly attest the slogan. BBC reports in 2019 establish conspicuous promotional use and contemporary criticism; the 2023 account documents rejection and displacement while acknowledging continued use. The onset, peak and fade are estimated bounds for this promotional moment, not measured first use or extinction.

entries.gloss: An exhortation to increase effort and continue working despite fatigue.

examples.text: Please hustle harder and finish the presentation today.

entries.rationale: The 2019 BBC account directly uses the phrase in its wake-work-sleep cycle. BBC reports in 2019 establish conspicuous promotional use and contemporary criticism; the 2023 account documents rejection and displacement while acknowledging continued use. The onset, peak and fade are estimated bounds for this promotional moment, not measured first use or extinction.

entries.gloss: A promotional ethos that treats continuous overwork as evidence of ambition.

examples.text: Thank you for completing the draft; your commitment to hustle culture is evident.
